A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MCTD paper, including Appendices A–E. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, algorithms, figures, and tables without material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original maze-navigation, cube-manipulation, and visual-planning experiments, together with scalability results and main-text and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons and appendix sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The tree-search procedure, guidance meta-actions, causal denoising, model architecture, and algorithms remain unchanged. The revised inverse-dynamics notation clarifies the already documented use of latent observations without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same pointmaze and antmaze navigate tasks, pointmaze stitch tasks, one-to-four-cube manipulation tasks, and medium/large visual pointmazes. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including Diffuser variants, Diffusion Forcing, greedy search, and the goal-inpainting Diffuser comparisons in Table 13. Rewritten baseline descriptions do not introduce new comparators.

E3.justification: Table 14 changes the reported default UCT coefficient from W = 1.141 to W = √2. This is a limited revision to a stated experimental setting, but v6's accompanying paragraph still specifies 1.141, leaving the actual setting unresolved. Neither PDF establishes that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The same greedy-search, guidance-set, subplan-count, causal-denoising, UCT, and jumpiness analyses remain, along with the stitch analysis and Figure 7 trajectory-collapse case study. The Table 14 setting-label revision adds no new analysis or outcome evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 retains five tasks per environment, ten seeds per model/task, and mean/standard-deviation reporting. Appendix A.5.7 retains three execution trials per AntMaze task/seed and selection of the best result; the revised wording does not change this practice.

E6.justification: The numerical outcomes in Tables 1–7 and 12–15, Figure 6 curves, and qualitative examples are unchanged. Table 14 revises a parameter label, not its success-rate, runtime, or search-count values. No new performance gain or loss is reported.

T1.justification: The probability factorizations, denoising formulation, training objective, and UCT formula retain their mathematical content. Replacing InvDyna and x-based notation with f_inv and explicit latent z variables clarifies existing mathematics; no new theorem, proof, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: integrating all four MCTS stages with diffusion planning through tree-rollout denoising, guidance meta-actions, and fast simulation, with improved inference-time scalability. Wording changes do not alter these claims.

C2.justification: The explanations involving systematic exploration, replanning, and local-control failures retain their meaning. Computational expense, limited search efficiency, short-training-horizon constraints, and difficult visual planning remain the same limitations despite rewritten discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix A.7.6 more explicitly identifies the position estimator's output as (x, y) coordinates predicted from latent states. The documented UCT default also changes in Table 14, although conflicting prose limits reproducibility. Other hyperparameter tables and code-access disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are unchanged. Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same distinctions from prior diffusion planners, Monte Carlo Guidance, and implicit diffusion-based search.

P1.justification: v6 extensively rewrites experimental-result prose and much of Appendix A, with additional edits to the abstract, discussion, and conclusion. Terminology and sentence construction are revised, and the cube reward constraints become a clearly labeled list. This is substantial language editing despite stable scientific content and section order.

P2.justification: All seven figures and fifteen tables are retained without redesigned visual evidence. Changes are limited to the Table 14 header, small spacing adjustments, and text reflow, including the bulleted reward constraints and shifted appendix page breaks.

improvement.justification: Clearer experimental descriptions, organized reward constraints, and explicit latent-state notation provide a modest overall readability gain. This is partially offset by the new disagreement between Table 14's √2 default and the accompanying 1.141 statement. The method and empirical support remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited.
